---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: RND_BACKLOG_CASH_RESERVE_CLEAN
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(LAG(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), 1), at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, at), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with a stock of prior R&D investment earn higher returns when they have balance-sheet cash support and are in a low-accrual state relative to their own history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior R&D spending is more likely to be productive when the firm has liquidity to continue investment without relying on accounting-supported earnings. The accrual leg uses within-firm state information rather than a plain cross-sectional Sloan sort, while the cash reserve leg adds a funding-quality filter.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: RND_ACCEL_UNVERIFIED_GLAMOUR
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ib), at), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with accelerating R&D intensity underperform when R&D-adjusted cash verification is persistently weak.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Rapid R&D acceleration can be interpreted as growth investment, but it may also be an overinvestment or glamour signal if cash flow plus R&D fails to support reported earnings. The interaction targets firms where intangible investment is ramping faster than cash economics can validate.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ORGANIC_INTAN_LIQUID_ACCRUAL_CLEAN
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))), SUMRANK(RATIO(che, at), NEG(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dp), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms dominated by organic R&D rather than goodwill earn higher returns when they have liquidity support and low working-capital accrual pressure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The first leg distinguishes internally generated intangible investment from acquisition-created goodwill. The second leg rewards firms that can fund organic innovation with cash reserves while avoiding working-capital accrual buildup, improving the separation of productive intangible capital from accounting noise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: GOODWILL_TAX_ACCRUAL_MASK
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(txach, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill-heavy firms underperform when positive tax-accrual adjustments coincide with a large earnings-cash-flow wedge.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Goodwill already makes acquisition performance difficult to verify, and tax-accrual timing can further obscure earnings quality. When both tax accruals and total accruals support reported income, acquisition-related intangible value may be overstated.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: INTAN_LOW_CHARGE_CASH_DECAY
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), MUL(RANK(NEG(RATIO(dpc, ADD(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oancf, at), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Recognized-intangible-heavy firms underperform when noncash charges are low and operating cash flow is deteriorating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: A large recognized intangible base should be validated either by cash generation or by disciplined amortization and impairment recognition. Low depreciation and amortization charges become more suspicious when operating cash flow is falling, suggesting delayed recognition of intangible asset weakness.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: RND_MOAT_RECEIVABLE_VALIDATED
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)), MUL(RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt))), RANK(RATIO(recch, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: R&D-intensive firms with industry-relative gross-margin strength earn higher returns when receivables are releasing cash.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gross-margin strength can indicate that R&D is creating pricing power or product differentiation, but the signal is more credible when sales are collected in cash. Positive recch reflects receivable cash release, helping distinguish a real innovation moat from accrual-supported revenue quality.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

response:
---CRITIQUE RND_BACKLOG_CASH_RESERVE_CLEAN---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical splice of two already-archived signals — RND_BACKLOG_LOW_ACCRUAL_STATE (identical first leg and identical TS_RANK accrual leg) and RND_CASH_RESERVE_ACCRUAL_CLEAN (the che/at + SUMRANK construction) — so it adds no new economic content beyond bolting an existing cash-reserve rank onto an existing backlog-accrual signal.

---CRITIQUE RND_ACCEL_UNVERIFIED_GLAMOUR---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: It is essentially the sign-reversed second leg of the archived RND_ACCEL_CASH_FUNDED (and a close cousin of RND_CUT_ACCRUAL_INFLATION), so it tests the same accel-times-cash-verification interaction already shown to give a positive FMB slope with a negative long-short alpha, and the rank-product form makes the short leg a mixture of "decelerating R&D" and "well-verified cash," muddying the stated glamour mechanism.

---CRITIQUE ORGANIC_INTAN_LIQUID_ACCRUAL_CLEAN---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The organic-R&D-minus-goodwill leg is verbatim from ORGANIC_INTAN_CASH_DOMINANCE and the WC-accrual leg is verbatim from ORGANIC_RND_WC_ACCRUAL_RECOVERY, with the only change being the addition of the che/at SUMRANK borrowed from RND_CASH_RESERVE_ACCRUAL_CLEAN — a cosmetic recombination of three already-evaluated components rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE GOODWILL_TAX_ACCRUAL_MASK---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is INTAN_TAX_ACCRUAL_SHARE_TRAP with intan swapped for gdwl and the normalized tax-accrual share replaced by a raw, unwinsorized txach/at, i.e. an intangible-leg substitution plus a noisier second leg rather than a substantively different hypothesis, and the triple rank product will concentrate the extremes in a small, unstable subsample.

---CRITIQUE INTAN_LOW_CHARGE_CASH_DECAY---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The "under-amortization relative to intangible base" leg is a genuinely distinct earnings-quality channel from the ib−oancf wedge used throughout the archive and its pairing with deteriorating OCF is coherent with the negative expected sign, though it overlaps RECOGNIZED_INTAN_UNDERCHARGE_ACCRUAL and INTAN_IMPAIRMENT_ACCRUAL_MASK and low dpc is partly a capital-intensity/industry proxy that should be checked as a confound.

---CRITIQUE RND_MOAT_RECEIVABLE_VALIDATED---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: It is RND_MOAT_CASH_VERIFIED with the persistent cash-wedge leg swapped for a single-period recch term — a weaker, noisier proxy that the archive already showed to be near-uninformative in RND_INVENTORY_BUILD_CASH_COLLECTION — and receivable cash release is as often a symptom of decelerating sales as of high-quality collection, so the "moat validation" story is not cleanly identified.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: RND_BACKLOG_REVENUE_PAYOFF_CLEAN
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(LAG(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), 1), at)), RANK(SUB(GROWTH(revt, 1), RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with a prior R&D backlog earn higher returns when that backlog is followed by revenue growth that is not offset by accrual-supported earnings.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the cash-reserve splice with a payoff-realization mechanism: past R&D should eventually show up in demand growth. Subtracting the earnings-cash-flow wedge penalizes cases where apparent revenue payoff is accompanied by accrual inflation.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: RND_ACCEL_MARGIN_FAIL_ACCRUAL
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), MUL(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with accelerating R&D intensity underperform when gross margins are deteriorating and earnings are accrual-supported.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This targets the glamour/overinvestment case more directly than a sign-flipped cash-verification leg: R&D is ramping while product economics are weakening. A positive earnings-cash-flow wedge suggests the failed payoff may be temporarily masked by accounting accruals.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ORGANIC_RND_GROSS_PAYOFF_QUALITY
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(ABS(SUB(revt, cogs)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)))), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with large sustained R&D relative to gross profit earn higher returns when earnings closely track cash flow.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This avoids reusing the organic-minus-goodwill and liquidity/accrual-leg splice, and instead asks whether the business can absorb a large R&D program without accounting distortion. Low absolute accrual noise helps distinguish deliberate long-horizon intangible investment from firms whose R&D burden is paired with unreliable earnings.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: GOODWILL_TAX_PAYABLE_REVERSAL
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(txp, at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill-heavy firms underperform when tax payables are falling, suggesting tax-accrual reversals or cash tax pressure after acquisition accounting.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This avoids the noisy triple product of goodwill, raw tax-accrual cash-flow adjustments, and total accruals. A decline in tax payables can indicate that prior tax-accrual support is reversing or that cash tax obligations are rising, which is especially concerning when acquisition goodwill makes earnings quality harder to verify.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: RND_MOAT_COLLECTION_STABILITY
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt)))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(recch, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: R&D-intensive firms with industry-relative gross-margin strength earn higher returns when receivable cash-flow effects are stable rather than noisy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces a single-period receivable release with a stability test, reducing the risk of rewarding decelerating sales or one-off collections. Productive innovation moats should produce margins without large swings in collection-related accruals.
